newsitem.title: INDIA: No reversal of credit growth slowdown-Indian bank.
newsitem.headline: No reversal of credit growth slowdown-Indian bank.

text.p: A slowdown in growth of Indian banks' credit to industry, seen last year, is still continuing, the chairman of one of the country's major banks said on Tuesday.
"There is little genuine rise in credit growth," Bank of Baroda (BOB) chairman K. Kannan told Reuters.
He said the paradox of banks being flush with funds and industrialists complaining about banks' reluctance to lend was real. "Banks are in a dilemma," he said.
Kannan said banks were no longer keen on deposit mobilisation as they had a problem of deployment of funds.
Banks were reluctant to lend to firms seeking loans.
"All the ratios are negative -- it's a story of rising inventories and receivables," Kannan said.
"People whom banks want to lend to (companies which are performing well) are raising funds from the debt market through debentures and through preference shares," he said.
"Many firms are seeking loans because of their problems," Kannan said. These firms are unable to forecast sales growth.
Banks were worried about adding to their portfolio of bad loans and hence the reluctance to lend to many firms, he said.
Banks, he said, were not happy to be flush with funds.
"We are not even getting savings bank rates by lending in the call market," he said, referring to the call money market where Bank of Baroda lends an average 7.0 billion rupees per day.
Bankers said some Indian firms are not doing well partly due to a global downtrend in prices of commodities and a reduction in Indian import duties, which make imports cheaper.
